summary: Guankong (1903–1989) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He taught at the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute and became a professor at the Buddhist Academy of China in 1957.

Gudo Wafu Nishijima (1919–2014) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1940–1946) and under Kodo Sawaki (~1940–1965), and held posts at the Ministry of the Treasury (~1946) and Japan Securities Finance.

Gudrun Bühnemann (born 1955) specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. She earned her doctorate at the University of Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner, and held research fellowships in Pune and Japan before becoming Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992.

Gudrun Melzer works in Indology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her Doktorgrad der Philosophie (2006) and PhD (2010) at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, studying under Jens-Uwe Hartmann.
Gunapala Dharmasiri specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held an academic post at the University of Ceylon, attested in 1991 and 2008.
Guo Jun works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Fuyan Buddhist Institute, Monash University, and the University of Sydney, and served as abbot at Mahabodhi Monastery (attested 2013).
Guohui Shi (born 1958) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Rissho University (~1997–2005) under Kenyu Mitomo, while also training under Sheng Yen (~1987–2009).

Gurinder Singh Mann (born 1949) specializes in religious studies and Indology. He studied at EFL University and Harvard University (~1987–1993), and held posts at Columbia University (~1988–1999) and the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1999–2015).

Gustaaf Houtman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London in 1990 under Richard Burghart, where he was attested as a Senior Teaching Fellow in 2014.

Gustav Haloun (1898–1951) was a Sinologist who studied under August Conrady (~1920–1923). He held posts at Charles University (~1926–1931), the University of Göttingen (~1931–1938), and as Professor of Chinese at the University of Cambridge (~1938–1951).

Gustav Roth (1916–2008) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Munich and Patna University, served at the University of Göttingen from 1965, and was Director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1982–1985).

Guy Claxton (born 1947) is a scholar affiliated with Buddhist studies. He founded the Sharpham College for Contemporary Buddhist Inquiry and served as Professor of the Learning Sciences at the University of Bristol (~1998–2008).

Guy G. Stroumsa (born 1948) works in religious studies and history. After studying at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Harvard University (~1974–1978), he held positions at Hebrew University (~1978–2009) and the University of Oxford (~2009–2014).

Guy Newland specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia in 1988 under Jeffrey Hopkins and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Central Michigan University (attested 1996–2010).
Gyatsho Tshering (1936–2009) was a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Calcutta. He founded the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, serving as its director from around 1972 to 1998.

Gyoei Fukuda (1867–1954) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tendai Sect University. He served as president of Taisho University (~1926–1944) and held teaching appointments at Toyo University and the University of Tokyo (1928).
Gyoko Iotani (born 1949) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Rissho University (~1968–1977), where he later served as an assistant professor (~1983–1993) and professor (~1993).
Gyosho Takahashi works in Buddhist studies. He held posts as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1992) and at Minobusan University (attested 1996).

Gyoshu Chujo is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1996) and as a professor in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Minobusan University (attested 2001).
Gyu Eon Jang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a professorship at Peking University and was an HK research professor at Geumgang University (attested 2015).
